recipes.title: Bobotie
recipes.dish_alt: A dish of bobotie with a golden baked egg-custard topping, served with turmeric yellow rice and chutney
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Mince and Custard Topping in the Pan
recipes.prep_alt: Curried mince topped with egg custard, cooking in a pan before baking

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: White bread slice, soaked in milk
Basmati or long-grain rice, to serve

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 170°C (340°F). Squeeze the excess milk from the soaked bread and mash it with a fork; set the bread and the reserved milk aside separately.
Ask an adult to help heat a little oil in a large pan and sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Stir in the curry powder and turmeric and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the mince and break it up with a spoon, cooking until no longer pink.
Stir in the mashed bread, chutney, raisins, almonds, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Simmer 5 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Spoon the mince mixture into a greased baking dish and press the top flat.
Whisk the egg with the milk for the custard and pour it evenly over the mince. Press the bay leaves into the surface.
Bake 30 minutes, until the custard is set and lightly golden on top.
While the bobotie bakes, cook the rice with a pinch of turmeric stirred into the cooking water until fluffy and golden.
Serve the bobotie hot with the yellow rice and extra chutney on the side.

recipes.title: Boerewors with Pap and Tomato-Onion Relish
recipes.dish_alt: Coiled boerewors sausage grilling over hot coals on a braai grate
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Raw Boerewors Coil, Ready for the Grill
recipes.prep_alt: A raw coiled boerewors sausage on a tray, ready to grill

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help heat a braai, grill, or grill pan to medium heat.
Grill the boerewors coil 20–25 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned all over and cooked through with no pink in the middle (or pan-fry if not grilling).

Meanwhile, make the relish: heat the oil in a pan, sauté the sliced onion until soft, then add the tomatoes, brown sugar, vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until jammy and thickened.
For the pap: bring the water and salt to a boil in a saucepan. Sprinkle in the mielie meal while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until thick and smooth. Stir in the butter.
Slice the boerewors and serve over the pap with the tomato-onion relish spooned generously on top.

recipes.title: Chicken Potjie
recipes.dish_alt: A red enamel potjie pot filled with chicken, carrots, and potatoes in a rich curried stew
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Browning the Meat Before Layering
recipes.prep_alt: Meat browning with onions in a cast-iron potjie pot before the stew is layered and simmered

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Chicken thighs, bone-in, skin-on, cut into pieces

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a potjie pot or heavy Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic until soft. Stir in the curry powder and coriander and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the chicken to the pot in a single layer, spice-side down.
Layer the potatoes, then the carrots, then the green pepper on top of the chicken, in that order — this is the golden rule of potjiekos: layer, don't stir.
Pour the stock gently down the side of the pot so it doesn't disturb the layers. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer very gently — low coals or the lowest stove setting — for 65–75 minutes without stirring, until the chicken and vegetables are tender.
Serve straight from the pot.

recipes.title: Bunny Chow
recipes.dish_alt: A hollowed quarter loaf of white bread filled with thick chicken curry, cut open to show the filling
recipes.prep_alt: Curry-filled hollowed bread loaf topped with sauce, served with a chopped vegetable sambal salad

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Crusty white bread loaf, quarter, hollowed
Sambal salad (grated carrot, chili, onion), to serve

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté the onion until soft, then add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the curry powder, turmeric, coriander, and garam masala, and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat in the spices, cooking until sealed on all sides.
Add the canned tomatoes, potato, and stock. Cover and simmer 25–30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through, the potato is tender, and the curry has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cut the bread quarters and hollow out the center of each, keeping the bread you remove for dunking.
Spoon the hot curry into the hollowed bread.
Serve with the sambal salad on the side and the reserved bread for scooping up the last of the curry.

recipes.title: Cape Malay Chicken Curry
recipes.dish_alt: A pot of golden chicken curry with potatoes, garnished with fresh coriander
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Chicken and Potato Simmering in the Spiced Sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Chicken curry with potatoes simmering in a pot on the stove

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Basmati or long-grain rice, to serve

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring occasionally, for about 10 minutes until deeply golden and caramelized.
Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods, and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the curry powder and turmeric, cooking 30 seconds more.
Add the chicken pieces, turning to coat them in the spice paste, and let them brown lightly for a couple of minutes.
Add the canned tomatoes, dried apricots, potato, and stock.
Cover and simmer 45–60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper. Fish out the cinnamon stick and cardamom pods before serving if you like.
Meanwhile, cook the rice with a pinch of turmeric stirred into the cooking water until fluffy and golden.
Serve the curry hot over the yellow rice.

recipes.title: Sosaties
recipes.time: 20 min (+2–4 hr marinate, overnight is best)
recipes.dish_alt: Grilled chicken sosatie skewers with peppers and apricot, served over pap
recipes.prep_alt: Rows of marinated meat skewers grilling over hot coals on an open-fire braai grate

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Green or yellow bell pepper, chunked

sections.heading: Steps
items: Whisk the apricot jam, vinegar, brown sugar, garlic, curry powder, turmeric, bay leaf, and oil together in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes. Let cool.
Thread the meat onto skewers, alternating with chunks of dried apricot, onion, and bell pepper.
Place the skewers in a dish, pour over the cooled marinade, cover, and refrigerate at least 2–4 hours (overnight gives the deepest flavor).
Ask an adult to help heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the skewers 10–12 minutes, turning occasionally and basting with extra marinade, until the meat is cooked through and lightly charred at the edges.
Serve hot over pap or rice.

recipes.title: Chakalaka and Pap
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of soft white maize pap with a spoonful of tomato-based chakalaka relish beside it
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Chakalaka Simmering on the Stove
recipes.prep_alt: A pot of chakalaka vegetable relish with tomatoes, peas, and beans simmering on the stovetop

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a pan and sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger until soft.
Add the carrots and bell pepper and cook 5 minutes until starting to soften.
Stir in the curry powder, paprika, and chili, and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 5–8 minutes until pulpy.
Stir in the baked beans, season with salt and pepper, and simmer 5 minutes more until heated through and slightly thickened.
Meanwhile, make the pap: bring the water and salt to a boil, whisk in the mielie meal, reduce the heat, cover, and simmer 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and smooth.
Serve the chakalaka spooned generously over the pap.

recipes.title: Malva Pudding (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: A square baking dish of malva pudding with glossy caramel sauce poured over the top
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Fresh from the Oven, Ready for the Sauce
recipes.prep_alt: A baked malva pudding in its pan, poked with holes ready to soak up the caramel sauce

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a small baking dish.
Whisk the egg and sugar together until pale, then beat in the melted butter and apricot jam.
In a small cup, stir the vinegar into the milk (it will look slightly curdled — that's fine) and stir in the vanilla.
Sift the flour, baking soda, and salt together, then fold into the egg mixture alternately with the milk mixture until just combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared dish and bake 25–30 minutes, until golden brown and a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean.
While the pudding bakes, make the sauce: warm the butter, sugar, cream, and vanilla together in a small saucepan until the sugar dissolves and it's steaming hot (don't let it boil).
As soon as the pudding comes out of the oven, poke holes all over the top with a skewer and slowly pour the warm sauce over so it soaks all the way through.
Let it rest 10 minutes to soak up the sauce, then serve warm, with custard or ice cream if you like.
